parts:
Hello Ayi

First of all I suggest that you slightly improve your initial data.frame. I would rearrange the data as follows (in excel or openoffice or gnumeric...):


Nr Sample.name Loci1_alele1 Loci_alele2 Loci2_alele1 Loci2_alele2 Loci3_alele1 Loci3_alele2

1 A 120 120 144 144 146 146
2 B 122 122 146 146 148 146
3 C 124 124 148 148 150 150
4 D 126 126 150 150 152 152
5 E 128 128 152 152 154 154

read the data to R

>mat<-read.csv("test_Ayi_best.csv", header=TRUE, sep=";", stringsAsFactors=TRUE)

> library(reshape)
to load the reshape package

>mat2<-melt(mat, id=c("Nr", "Sample.name"))
create a new data.frame preserving the first two columns and rearranging the data

> mat2<-cbind(mat2, colsplit(mat2$variable, split="_", names=c("Loci", "Alele")))

to separate the Loci tag from the alele tag

 > mat2<-mat2[,c(1:2,5:6,4)]
to reorganize the data

> mat3<-cast(mat2, Nr+Sample.name+Loci~Alele, value="value", sum)
to reshape the data as you want it...

   Nr Sample.name  Loci alele1 alele2
1   1           A Loci1    120    120
2   1           A Loci2    144    144
3   1           A Loci3    146    146

9   3           C Loci3    150    150

12  4           D Loci3    152    152
13  5           E Loci1    128    128

It worked for me...

Best regards
